title: Sector (CP 201): independent retail wages
summary: Choose the wage scale according to company group, workforce size, function, and experience. The official grid effective since May 2026 avoids announcing a uniform minimum wage for all retail.
body: The page is effective May 1, 2026, after a 2% indexation. For group 1, sales staff of companies with fewer than 20 workers, at zero years of experience, gross monthly minimums are 2,037.81 euros in category 1, 2,094.97 euros in category 2, 2,126.02 euros in category 3, and 2,258.40 euros in category 4.

First identify the group and category corresponding to actual tasks. Administrative staff have separate tables. In the group 1 table for sales staff of companies with 20 or more workers, category 1 employees move to category 2 after six months seniority in the company. Also check the applicable guaranteed average minimum monthly wage.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Sector (CP 202): food retail wages
summary: Use the July 2026 grid and distinguish between sales staff, administrative staff, managers, and students.
body: The official grid is effective July 1, 2026 after a 1% indexation. In general scale B, sales staff of group 1, ordinary employees with no seniority, gross monthly minimums are 2,099.26 euros in category I, 2,216.43 euros in category II, 2,322.79 euros in category III, and 2,462.68 euros in category IV.

Group 2 and managers have their own tables. For group 1 students, the July 2026 grid applies notably 75% at age 16, 82.5% at age 17, and 87.5% at age 18. Check the exact committee or sub-committee before using an amount in a job offer.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Sector (CP 311): large retail business wages
summary: The grid cross-references professional experience and company seniority. The stated wage must specify category and working hours regime.
body: The grid effective July 1, 2026 incorporates 2% indexation and presents a 35-hour weekly regime. For an employee age 21 or older in category I, with no experience, the gross monthly starting wage is 2,197.30 euros; the one-year seniority column shows 2,217.89 euros.

Monthly amounts apply to part-time on a pro rata basis. The SPF clarifies that its indexation calculations may differ slightly from sector amounts calculated from base amounts. Confirm the payroll calculation corresponding to the function and recognized experience.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Sector (CP 312): department store wages
summary: Check category, experience, and seniority before setting wages. Sector (CP 312) provides a specific formula to convert the wage scale to part-time.
body: The grid effective May 1, 2026 incorporates 2% indexation. For execution staff category 1, age 21 and over, with no experience, the gross monthly minimum at hiring is 2,238.97 euros. The one-year seniority column shows 2,256.54 euros.

For part-time, the page provides an hourly rate equal to the category wage scale amount divided by 151.66. Monthly compensation equals the wage scale multiplied by monthly hours, then divided by 151.66. The SPF notes possible slight variations due to its indexation method; verify the sector amount used in payroll.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Sector (CP 302): Horeca wages and student wages
summary: Classify the Horeca position in the correct job category before announcing the wage. Standard wages and flexi-job pay are separate regimes.
body: The official sheet effective September 1, 2026 presents standard wages on a 38-hour-per-week basis. At zero years of function, gross hourly minimums are notably 15.2097 euros for categories I and II, 15.2977 euros for III, 15.9698 euros for IV, and 16.8849 euros for V. The minimum monthly wage for categories I and II at this level is 2,504.53 euros.

Wages then depend on years of function. For a student contract, the percentage of the category wage scale is 70% at age 15, 80% at age 16, 90% at age 17, and 100% at age 18. These percentages do not exempt checking whether tasks and schedules are permitted for the young person.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Retail: opening hours 5 AM to 9 PM in 2026
summary: The official page updated in August 2026 in principle authorizes retail stores to open from 5 AM to 9 PM, seven days a week. Separately check staff work rules.
body: The November 10, 2006 law was amended by the July 20, 2026 law. According to the current SPF Economy presentation, most stores can open from 5 AM to 9 PM and remain open seven days a week. The old general requirement for weekly store closure should no longer be cited as current rule.

Night stores typically follow a 6 PM to 7 AM window and may face municipal restrictions. Horeca is excluded from this opening-hours legislation. For mixed activity, the SPF indicates the entire business is excluded if Horeca activity reaches at least 40% of annual revenue. Public opening does not suffice to authorize paid Sunday work.

owner.name: SPF Économie, P.M.E., Classes moyennes et Énergie

title: Sunday work and staff rest
summary: Identify the exemption permitting Sunday work and provide compensatory rest. Staff rules differ from store opening.
body: The March 16, 1971 law in principle prohibits Sunday work, article 11. Its article 66 notably authorizes employment in hotels, restaurants, and bars. In retail, article 14 generally permits work from 8 AM to noon; full-day services require another exemption, notably those of the December 3, 1987 royal order.

Compensatory rest is in principle granted within the following six days. Per article 16, it lasts a full day if the service exceeds four hours and a half-day otherwise. Retail in recognized tourist centers can employ each worker up to 39 Sundays per calendar year, under article 14, section 2 conditions. Also check sector bonuses and minor-specific restrictions.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Horeca: suppression of register-linked reduction
summary: No longer budget NSSO reduction for fixed Horeca workers from July 2026 recruitment. NSSO confirms elimination with no transition.
body: NSSO 2026/3 instructions announce the elimination of this target-group reduction as of July 1, 2026, per the program law of May 30, 2026 published June 1. Subsequent developments on the page describe the old system and no longer constitute aid available for the third quarter 2026.

The eliminated system tied the benefit to an approved register in the establishments concerned and daily recording of work start and end times via SCE/GKS or alternative system. It explicitly distinguished these records from Dimona, which remained necessary. Do not present the old timekeeping tied to this reduction as a formality still allowing aid access.

title: Horeca extras: contingents and flat-rate contributions
summary: An extra is hired for a maximum two consecutive days. Check worker and employer contingents before applying NSSO flat rates.
body: NSSO 2026/3 instructions limit casual work to a fixed-term contract or clearly defined work of maximum two consecutive days with the Horeca employer or user. Beyond that, all related services must be declared as ordinary work. The favorable regime requires available days in both contingents: 50 days per calendar year for the worker and 200 for the employer.

From the third quarter 2026, the flat-rate basis is 11.52 euros per commenced hour, capped at 69.12 euros in hourly Dimona, or 69.12 euros per day in daily Dimona. The basis is increased by 8% for workers. These amounts serve to calculate contributions, not set wages. Consult Horeca@work and use adapted declaration; contingent excess triggers ordinary contributions.

title: Flexi-jobs: controls and wages in September 2026
summary: Check individual flexi-job access and apply sector wages. The July 2026 Horeca amount is replaced by the September amount.
body: In principle, the non-pensioned candidate must have worked at least 80% in quarter T-3. Also check incompatibilities with employer and related businesses, as well as temporary exclusion after reduction from 100% to 80%. Conclude the required framework contract then the flexi contract, declare in Dimona FLX, and record services. Temps workers follow specific arrangements described by NSSO.

Since September 1, 2026, the Horeca minimum is 12.11 euros/hour plus 0.93 euros vacation allowance, equaling 13.04 euros/hour. The stated Horeca ceiling is 21 euros/hour excluding vacation allowance, or 22.61 euros with allowance. In other sectors, including retail, base pay respects the job wage scale and its ceiling is in principle 150% of minimum. The tax ceiling for non-pensioned is 18,440 euros for 2026.

title: Tips and service: NSSO basis
summary: Tip-based compensation requires specific payroll treatment. It does not exempt the employer from declarations and contributions.
body: NSSO 2026/3 instructions provide flat daily payments for workers compensated entirely or partially by tips or service in relevant functions. The flat rates were adjusted July 1, 2026. For exclusively tip-based compensation, multiply days by applicable flat rate then increase the basis by 8%.

For mixed compensation, compare the flat basis to sums and benefits owed by employer, increased by 8%, per page rules. Year-end bonus remains subject to ordinary contributions. Identify the exact function and its DmfA code; clarify to the candidate the fixed portion and service distribution method, without presenting tips as automatically exempt.

title: Horeca: 450 voluntary overtime hours
summary: The Horeca regime applicable in 2026 provides up to 450 voluntary hours per calendar year under conditions. Prior agreement and a declared cash register are required.
body: The specific regime of article 31/1 of the November 16, 2015 law, presented by SPF in its current version, targets Sector (CP 302) and requires an SCE declared to tax authorities at each place of business. Since the reform effective April 1, 2026, the quota reaches 450 annual voluntary hours. Limits remain 11 hours per day and 50 hours per week.

The prior written agreement lasts one year, with automatic renewal and written termination with one month notice. These hours do not generate compensatory rest. Of the 450 hours, 360 do not carry overtime pay and 90 do. Parallel use of the non-recoverable Horeca credit does not permit exceeding a total of 360 hours exempt from overtime pay. Additional conditions apply to part-time.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Students: NSSO contingent of 650 hours
summary: Check student balance before reserving hours in Dimona. The social contingent does not replace student contract or sector wage scale.
body: NSSO 2026/3 instructions provide 650 hours per calendar year for solidarity contribution application. The contingent covers actually worked hours, all employers combined. Hours paid without actual service, notably holidays or sick leave, are not counted, but their payment remains subject to solidarity contribution.

Hours are reserved in Dimona STU based on a signed contract. Have the balance checked before simultaneous engagement at multiple stores or establishments. Combination with 50 occasional Horeca days is provided; distinguish STU and EXT declarations and their contribution bases. After a diploma obtained in June, NSSO still admits student regime until September 30 if employment genuinely remains student and does not constitute a disguised trial.

title: Student contract and light work from age 15
summary: Formalize each student engagement in writing no later than at start of service. Since May 2026, certain 15-year-olds still subject to full-time schooling obligation can perform light work.
body: A student contract is a fixed-term, individual contract, established in two copies and signed no later than at start of service. It must contain mandatory mentions. The first three actually worked days constitute the trial period. After 12 uninterrupted months with the same employer, ordinary contract rules apply.

Since May 4, 2026, young people age 15 still subject to full-time schooling obligation can be hired only for authorized light work. The list notably includes reception assistance, restocking, sales assistance, and certain light cleaning tasks, without specific training or mechanical equipment. Do not extend this list to all kitchen or service positions; check article 7.15 conditions of the labor law.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Horeca: training staff on food hygiene
summary: Provide training or instructions adapted to food tasks from staff onboarding. Those responsible for self-inspection must master HACCP principles.
body: Guide G-023 published on the AFSCA website, part 1, section 21, incorporates the requirement of European regulation 852/2004, annex II, chapter XII. Food-handling staff must be supervised and receive instructions and/or training adapted to their activity. Those responsible for guide implementation must receive training appropriate to HACCP principles.

To hire kitchen or dining staff, verify hygiene competencies and plan establishment-specific instructions. The guide recommends adapting language and content to staff level, keeping instructions accessible, and supplementing learning with daily corrections. This section does not require every candidate have a single diploma or universal training duration.

owner.name: Agence fédérale pour la sécurité de la chaîne alimentaire

title: Alcohol sales: verify customer age
summary: Train sales and service staff in age verification. Sales age thresholds should not be confused with staff hiring age.
body: The SPF Public Health page, updated June 23, 2026, prohibits selling, serving, or offering alcohol to those under 18. Beer and wine are permitted from age 16 if they contain no added spirits or spirit flavor. The professional must verify age with official ID and refuse sale if in doubt.

Incorporate these checks in onboarding students and checkout or service staff. This source addresses the recipient’s age; it does not provide a general prohibition on hiring servers under 18. To assign a minor to service, separately check permitted tasks, schedules, and young worker protection rules.

owner.name: SPF Santé publique, Sécurité de la Chaîne alimentaire et Environnement

title: Hotel reception: organizing night work
summary: To hire a night receptionist, define the schedule and verify the procedure for introducing night work at the hotel.
body: Since June 1, 2026, night work is in principle permitted in sectors subject to labor law. Its general definition remains the 8 PM to 6 AM period. This permission does not excuse compliance with work rules, rest, CBAs, and special protections.

A regime with night services targets habitual work between 8 PM and 6 AM with always services between midnight and 5 AM. Article 38 provides for a special procedure, including prior consultation per applicable arrangements. Before publishing the offer, verify the actual regime, work rules, and sector benefits. Separately check protections for young workers.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale

title: Young workers: breaks and schedule limits
summary: Check young worker limits before assigning a minor to store closing or Horeca service. The schedule must also account for other employers.
body: The SPF sheet in principle sets a maximum of eight hours per day and forty hours per week, respecting 38 hours effective or average weekly duration. Time at multiple employers is added together. A 30-minute break is due if work exceeds 4.5 hours; beyond six hours, rest reaches in principle one hour.

Between two work days, provide at least 12 consecutive hours of rest. Work between 8 PM and 6 AM is in principle prohibited; exemptions must be verified for the activity and age. Even when an exemption permits Sunday, the young person in principle cannot work more than one Sunday in two without prior authorization from Labor Law Enforcement. Young people age 15 still subject to full-time schooling obligation are subject to specific additional conditions.

owner.name: SPF Emploi, Travail et Concertation sociale
